title: 4 signs it’s time to change your boss
description: Work is the closest thing most adults have to a full-time identity . Strip away sleep, and roughly half of our waking lives are spent working . If you take a conservative estimate—40 to 50 hours a week, across four to five decades—you end up with well over 80,000 hours on the job. And yet, the most salient feature of work is not how many hours we devote to it, but rather how we experience it, which varies wildly. For some, it resembles what the sociologist Max Weber once described as a “ calling ,” a source of meaning and even a kind of secular transcendence. For others, it’s closer to what Karl Marx labeled alienation : a draining, joyless routine that disconnects effort from purpose.
